00E7EFC89AB343E58AF9BDF33874D240.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

C2529B2114D544478051D191FCFE2CBE.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

97FD875BDF7F47359BFFAF08F93366DD.description: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.

CC3D169F9FFE4CF2BA40F372EC3090C9.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.

7C050AB85A4541B0A4AA358085A44249.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

B6D456B028A043A1A5C92DA5C0126063.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

7D2B47EA3EE840B7804C49DC8D9E63AA.description: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.

61B7A31248A542DF90B902F71BE95F57.description: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.

23D1978B3C8D4CA5A3900AAB838535EA.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

4EEACB8902454DAE90F675A6D9A18649.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2—3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

4D85685452E7472CA87FAF66A246EE8D.description: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.

A9D9E82AF62B442FB03AF5126FCEB111.description: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.

3229F29E8F65485D829C3484F4A6FEE7.description: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

A393D05100204DED84702CE8A13E6F54.description: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.

796224D0A7E648EEA5D6ED1372F8D04D.description: Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

A18541E0B2B045EE96C80BE37E0FEEC0.description: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.

E05D67CC89EA4AC3B7563EE7AAECEDD4.description: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.

06FCAC96DE214B41B0BAC01ABBBDACB3.description: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.

1C9E7361CAF4489CBA8FCB71220DA7B5.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

06F267083A8C4E9E95442003417669B3.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

05099DB6CA2E4FC8AF6DE8A1F92CA2DA.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

01DF49225708418ABC2A90F07C4AE1B9.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

A6576970053A477095EF8A574BE4428C.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

7C72FBCB3232446495D388BEF9ED168E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

DA510232DF78479FAFD48CCDEBFB6193.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

E20B1CEB8FD04055B2FC5ACCEB603446.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

A5F489E44EE74FE39807FE09681118B7.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

D6DFF17DDEFE437EAA387390F59CE7EF.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

278A30EF785C48328CB3AAA5F263FB85.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: North Dakota Science Content Standards

FD8364C0DFE60131EBDD68A86D17958E.description: Identify scientific advances that changed popular beliefs (e.g., Earth was center of universe, world was flat, man was incapable of flight)

FD82D0C0DFE60131EBDB68A86D17958E.description: Identify a variety of careers in the field of science

FD823BB0DFE60131EBD968A86D17958E.description: Students understand the history and nature of science.

FD81FCB0DFE60131EBD868A86D17958E.description: Standard 8: History and Nature of Science

FD81B950DFE60131EBD768A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which science and technology have greatly improved human lives (e.g., food quality and quantity, transportation, health, sanitation, communication)

FD811C00DFE60131EBD568A86D17958E.description: Identify consequences of natural and humaninduced environmental changes (e.g., erosion, tsunami, deforestation)

FD809450DFE60131EBD368A86D17958E.description: Students understand relations between science and personal, social, and environmental issues.

FD7FFCD0DFE60131EBD168A86D17958E.description: Explain how an invention may lead to other inventions

FD7FA950DFE60131EBD068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of technology on people and the environment (e.g., new construction, oil drilling, electric cars)

FD7F0F50DFE60131EBCE68A86D17958E.description: Students understand relations between science and technology.

FD7E6780DFE60131EBCC68A86D17958E.description: Identify tools that are used to study the universe (e.g., telescopes, space probes, satellites, space craft)

FD7DC270DFE60131EBCA68A86D17958E.description: Identify components of our solar system (e.g., planets, moons, Sun)

FD7D4120DFE60131EBC868A86D17958E.description: Compare fossil evidence to existing organisms

FD7CFEA0DFE60131EBC768A86D17958E.description: Use characteristics to classify Earth's materials (i.e. rocks, soil)

FD7CB940DFE60131EBC668A86D17958E.description: Identify slow and rapid processes (e.g., wind, water, waves, ice, volcano, earthquake) that are constantly changing Earth's surface

FD7C1EB0DFE60131EBC468A86D17958E.description: Describe how as water condenses small droplets of water form clouds and fog

FD7B9C10DFE60131EBC268A86D17958E.description: Students understand the basic concepts and principles of earth and space science.

FD7B01C0DFE60131EBC068A86D17958E.description: Identify adaptations that help plants and animals survive and grow in their environment

FD7AAB70DFE60131EBBF68A86D17958E.description: Classify plants and animals according to common physical characteristics

FD7A0E00DFE60131EBBD68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that an organism's pattern of behavior is related to the nature of the organism's environment (e.g., the availability of food, space, and resources)

FD798540DFE60131EBBB68A86D17958E.description: Identify behaviors of animals as instinctive or learned

FD78DF60DFE60131EBB968A86D17958E.description: Students understand the basic concepts and principles of life science.

FD784CA0DFE60131EBB768A86D17958E.description: Identify ways friction or burning produces heat (e.g., magnifying glass, carpet burn, sunburn)

FD780C80DFE60131EBB668A86D17958E.description: Explain how the pitch of a sound is related to the rate of vibrations.

FD77CAC0DFE60131EBB568A86D17958E.description: Describe how the path of light changes (i.e., reflected, absorbed, or allowed to pass through) when it encounters a variety of objects

FD773E60DFE60131EBB368A86D17958E.description: Identify the effects forces may have when applied to objects (i.e., start, stop, change direction)

FD76ADF0DFE60131EBB168A86D17958E.description: Explain that matter is made up of parts that are too small to see without magnification

FD766A90DFE60131EBB068A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between the mass of an object and the sum of its parts.

FD762780DFE60131EBAF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the forms in which water appears when heated and cooled (i.e., water vapor, liquid, solid)

FD759BC0DFE60131EBAD68A86D17958E.description: Students understand the basic concepts and principles of physical science.

FD750090DFE60131EBAB68A86D17958E.description: Use scientific tools (i.e., thermometers, rulers, balances) during simple investigations

FD74B7B0DFE60131EBAA68A86D17958E.description: Conduct simple investigations to answer questions based on observations

FD7471E0DFE60131EBA968A86D17958E.description: Review and ask questions about the scientific investigations of others

FD742A80DFE60131EBA868A86D17958E.description: Abilities Necessary to do Scientific Inquiry

FD73DE30DFE60131EBA768A86D17958E.description: Students use the process of science inquiry.

FD8483A0DFE60131EBE168A86D17958E.description: Explain changes in the real world using a model (e.g., erosion, volcano, stream table, wing designs for airplanes)

FD83EC50DFE60131EBDF68A86D17958E.description: Students understand the unifying concepts and processes of science.

document.title: North Dakota Mathematics Content Standards

1726DD2CE71343AEB6C50DA324A26780.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

F9D99DD2B3474DD581CE3AC46D6B8A47.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

38115778344E41E4AEA64C2DB4675B1F.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.
comments: For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.
For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant.
8EBF62CC69A64B749454AF93BABE6E47.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.

EA4D849411AF4B6B96F3D00B4ECBD29B.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

D95FED3386944E13BB03F77D01A8EF44.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

comments: For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?
E22B0F926D3548ABB79AE3255A595C09.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.

45D7628830D24C3BBE589B9A7F1DB14E.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.
comments: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

1D3B96EE992F4DD4B6190122E1B3F39D.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

EC8FB98EE8934D4E9751068CCCC5CFB4.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

BDB326B3FCA04D1B8BA5FAEF6996B01D.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems

8709FDEF94FC4DD2AE8B14EE43EFAA8C.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

1EC446FD780E4FBDBD71FCEF7CA18C7D.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

A46537BD40204CBE9E1A4F5A3D39AF25.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

8412BBD03B0E4B7FA5A9E28D8EF3BBA1.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

06099BF1B8564192B1FB2282E0816320.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model

comments: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.
E6A74A1084324E18AFB8FE9C2BE53969.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

comments: For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.
6CBBA3A4F7724BC588AEC06604D363B3.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

C30A911665344FA681D916E7B3AAD33C.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

660844C9999F47F2A0B9CECF87C3FCEA.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

263AF29DD7244FFD8FF0ED5D28468743.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

134025E4E5DD4D918ED344B5A25CBCF4.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data

9A6AACE97D294A4984355C29353D11AE.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

696E5B1E591746DD8F3AF7A68C35C5C8.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

D851D384488D4B89816D47FF95AEA747.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

64F5ABDFEDC14251B0006D10E862CE08.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

81A87ADA116746D28EC0E019542F7112.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies

51DF99FDD4234EFEB903C0E677FD699C.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.
comments: For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

20F78F48DE5848A2A64D78A5B1614CE3.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

C9AC89F0EACA493F947D2BDB86E978C6.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments

7D44F9D33D5A431595B10DEFCABA32AD.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

4F9BB48570A44160ADE9C2802BF35963.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

B55003EC41964626A8226ABA50BA54EF.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

7C12E22C5A24488FBF7F7C68E433F53B.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

EB4C6A42170C4608A2E132B6A27A680B.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.
comments: Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

6942A22C397540DB80332750A5B701FD.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

328215DE697C477B9C00F071965C8AE9.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

BFAA6E917D834B1FAE1BA57133ABC89D.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

91E33D7B63A54C698C97DC66483451BE.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

18C21ACE931C458D91752375B7BDC686.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

704D4967E3C549FFB048694042BC4508.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

FCAEDD27DA9C4B05B6B9F3337123BDB5.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

EFA788D01BE445C788A05279BEC68EBF.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

2600DE6AD2BA43ACBF5510BAECD606B0.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

95643DEA2A9B4160BE73F85C69611519.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
6EA602406D334D18A18053B714315C2E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
111CF0538D3949CAB290FF47B0C411D7.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

2DA33E68F0F84902B1A94D17BB6EDF04.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

68B1BCDD201C4D46898B6F1C0028FDB4.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

1FD9D6484E5949218C2FD7DF908B5D6B.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft., and improvised units.

382D78B5A4184602B9093E836300F41E.description: A solid figure, which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes, is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

C86D4EDD5FF44D17B871AA093EDC61EF.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube," is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

BAF07177CAA543C0B5018B4C923319BB.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

66568EA7EE6C4AA5857651962B83C084.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

15705C81579E45F2A9E028AFF6352F01.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

18EE689DA59143C89C26650E4D8FFC48.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system. Use these conversions in solving multi-step, real world problems.

4AEF9AA6F819424BA2C715324910B3C4.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

D68DF03F2A1E44A48FE9C5591C694594.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

5643431929F04DCEAC053BCD5B59EC96.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction, and compute such quotients.

118EDB301D974C6A9D3B7387E9112044.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number, and compute such quotients.

3839CCC7F09A491E9A1E5F410329EAFC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

4CB5175285B8494CA7CF856C312E3582.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

86F0A4676C314DD5BABDC8935A246DAA.description: Relating the principle of fraction equivalence a/b = (n×a)/(n×b) to the effect of multiplying a/b by 1.

0C28A7B41C234423801D3BB5B179AFB8.description: Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number (recognizing multiplication by whole numbers greater than 1 as a familiar case) Explaining why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.

D3D7507F71024A5AB95EC6123DA10C67.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. D143BDB3914C47C4A14407004EB61106.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.

0878770781554FC693FF9E2FBAA840E5.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

CCB524254C234EB7BBE3964F14BA0F4A.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

D4D45B862FCB4848AFB9F7A0F80CC554.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

EAA9EB747C2147828DC5FEC9F699B44D.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole, including cases of unlike denominators, by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

21BD06C699674899B668F43F2980BDF1.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.

0A1BD06B9F714803913A69E5C2B9BFC8.description: Using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction, add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths. 31F5B7A1B87C4B5F9ECC0CBBFFAFA8D2.description: Using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division, find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors. 4E497115667342C2B776978DC48DA261.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using strategies flexibly, including the standard algorithm.

9FFD65D902004C23B0E53088EBEFB845.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

8497BDA72B104790878DC0FDBB4F8C3F.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

DA71626005B54B128D9B7EE40DCFA984.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

4976AA3F2934401AB64CC68520078BA5.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

Explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

5162A20FD37A43A991A64829FFC59676.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

F9559394EB424944ACA5148EE15DFF54.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

071C801A794842A8BFDC3E8C8B73E275.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns. Graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. Use the graph to verify relationships.

4EDB801DCC9D435C981CC8F493E29BA4.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

00A79043311D4A89A2507E5D3A050E3E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

26A1CF03E70C42BDB3D66557E94E2F81.description: Look for and make use of structure.

034DA798B34E4F3FB67B022B58737005.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2B8A25386C074266B5BC296999ABEF16.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Dakota Mathematics Content Standards

72CC727B418E44988F306DE92BC5DEA7.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

C875DADC17FC48AC84689E45C6343FCF.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

CA5E3017492145D88B4DE12A35A470D9.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

39A50B3E99FB46F780A187347B7CD5CF.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

1AB011CEA87E4453AF78686E85E8B817.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiements, and observational studies

A7474096DFE94B128F32475AB7F33ABC.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.

471E678582D249189C9EC6EED1B45558.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

596D4C27AD7549E993C76CAF77204F0D.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

7924121DD5DE436BB0109F76E1F370F8.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

B0784BC7EED04FBDA955D6B320D90B44.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

DD274DFC969D419EA7E65C9B7AD747CE.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

D240A4E65516468E83BAE76F8D277830.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

5186C0350B084961BB6BCF691FD72C03.description: Use tables, graphs, verbal descriptions, and equations to interpret and sketch the key features of a function modeling the relationship between two quantities.

11EEF355F5C945B289B7823118E80BFB.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

8681034541924559A9A2F16A7D5CF2CA.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

F5DBF27BD8034BA0A8A6DC323CD9BEF1.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

817A588D6EE64318B1777EB5AAF695A4.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

C960A3A8B0454B9D9E44D0CA7FE65C0E.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

D89DFD5898074222B5B668F79630549D.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

41463A4201AD475A800B3BB3818766AF.description: Find the inverse of a matrix, if it exists, and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

7CF5BA21D47943248C41C9A1BFBC5F48.description: Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation.

5DA3E894E2264B85ABF3899C5DD52651.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

4C584D9B028045CA8A6E825FC13E503C.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

F1555E26AEE348F4B80E9814BF159A30.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

2AE6D44888874988AE216CBADE809E6D.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions.(+) Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

2A64482A787A49D89287CB341A6FEF99.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

82D890993B4A4E4D94EA6B06BBA628AD.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

4E6CF573BF944762ABF111DC26324E47.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

912DF1F194EF4341974AF9E50B24147B.description: Rearrange formulas to isolate a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

C39416188C004373B703B0F8D18B14D6.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

10B86D53EB3B4F2FA6D6387F643CE96E.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities. Graph equations on coordinate axes with appropriate labels and scales.

00F7F8977FAA493EA5E0EAAF76C62542.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

C9C1CD4CBE094AECA6A9156145E370F0.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

DAED2479E56743CFB15AB5A1A7B075E7.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions. Understand that rational expressions form a system comparable to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression.

79CE8B82EE494BEB8C917A2D505FF453.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

326BE3E9D7FE4421B3FB83D3768BA457.description: Apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n.

B5BDAE3DA8E64EB7B1DF09025C13779A.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

9D757BDA41C04EDBA02795F90B7C11D9.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available. Use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

E62FB01C04A046AB9C771B82A8607666.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

004685CAF5F2432CA4709C622390F969.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials. Understand that polynomials form a system comparable to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

BAD2E96E84D041CCA5BAB1763D8B52CC.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

E544A2B5B498471C973F6788F264C130.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform exponential expressions.

5C2B3A50CD474A508D830CF98DBF07E7.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to produce an equivalent expression.

AD87258D7913456097005BB200C148C4.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

AB45127DB3B04A13BD9B288716730919.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

C3B11034F45543B3877002CD3096C4CC.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

5181230D93794775AE27161A7FD3C0D3.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

AFBCE18035B649CFA5DCB64E9E61EB0D.description: Interpret complicated expressions by examining one or more of their parts as a single entity.

24534F248818452B8D1881B8153E2F11.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

F5044A68961D403FB982A896DC68CE6F.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

4D197B77E7A5487C888AE3CF72EC88B5.description: Understand a 2 × 2 matrix as a transformation of the plane. Interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

8EFC2BCB39474CC890304E0B17519755.description: Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Understand a matrix as a transformation of vectors.

E131CC864B354102BF9F0E4CAE0E1EB3.description: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

7C8CA0D94C424EA999959B5FABAF1BA0.description: Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

4658E5F1FA36499DA7C6080525CBCB90.description: Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

55FDC05FE11D49F6A11207ED1BE3F314.description: Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices.

8AC7575536E1425FBF0F58C6D2C2E16F.description: Use matrices to represent and manipulate data.

E0E69617B21F4D1EA0479C47BD1BE5A7.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications

64EFAB06494B45628B62D0BB3B089DFA.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

D791E739A4D34DF6AD9B8B5DD380D0E9.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction. Use the components to perform scalar multiplication (e.g., as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>)).

BB7B7539FE6745FC9CB6C8712306EC8A.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

2DEC24C5769443C4BD8BD1745CE592BF.description: Understand that vector subtraction v – w is defined as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order and use the components to perform vector subtraction.

1AD8E0E3E5774ECE8A58F30456039636.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

3B1A5F366240489292179672F0F62E39.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

96731EB8C5394617A5F704C3DA72D1BF.description: Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

27840C7B793A4B65922AD7D730B2C828.description: Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

C5F2EB1CFBED4867B4DD6D4A55C63A48.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

8956088393C543A884B477800AF382E4.description: Represent and model with vector quantities

1433EC6F61104DF4B6CE8460F998965B.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to determine the number of zeros for polynomial functions. Find all solutions to a polynomial equation.

8D56CF92E5AC4E08A6C5180C5059AAB1.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

63FC18F2628E429CBA99AB764F103AC2.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

26E70130C9E848A9A4EC9EA1C30C3C8B.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations

4F91BA4ABE1D42A89174E16A2CAFDA8D.description: Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

D9874019802747DA84F504544F4B3C8A.description: Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers). Find moduli (absolute value) of a complex number. Explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

D2440D09C3A7413ABAC9E9BF5C824247.description: Use conjugates to find quotients of complex numbers.

716E0AF5B4194F3E802DBD02F1CC3944.description: Use the definition i² = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

1ACAC5A15AF5476C9F4742FFCBF51432.description: Know there is an imaginary number i, such that i² = −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi where a and b are real. Understand the hierarchal relationships among subsets of the complex number system.

47C7023B81A448B586DC6AF727806BA2.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers

8A27566BE4664E2BB22A98C4A3779BC2.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

DC3BDFCD91AF48479979E4506E3F8126.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems (e.g., unit analysis). Choose and interpret units consistently in formulas. Choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

C25806E73D8246DEB7DE6B18C75B089D.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems

6BCFDD81E9264A3EA3D5325327E3D40B.description: Perform basic operations on radicals and simplify radicals to write equivalent expressions.

A6174E95E5FE4468A5C565E33D539210.description: Demonstrate that the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational, and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

96DA830B55CB43EAAC6EB78120DF8F62.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational numbers

document.title: North Dakota Mathematics Content Standards

6B0F0AF951754728AF4B77F260532CF1.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

1AE5B5BE52DB4B7595BBD36E71DDB1CE.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals. Draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

6130C443FBD242C89527928379A57BFC.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

6B3E24A0B43A42F0AF2716CCBAE84975.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths. Find an unknown side length. Exhibit rectangles with the same perimeter and different area or with the same area and different perimeters.

4CEAB1E1B34F4873819F4F97BFF866A7.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

14EDD49AC03D4911BD0745FE5ABC7CCF.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

2FE6D091E8CB4E548EEE1038EA4F8E82.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

80B5314BEA1E412D8BCA93EA1C9841FF.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

ACF5421D894043A0AC3BCAA9E8840056.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

54174314B90B46A4ACF2A38CE72E219C.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

3D5A1DBB6BE14D0EAF83B8BE064F0278.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

7810D4B300164EC7B114735A59087422.description: A plane figure, which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares, is said to have an area of n square units.

6C3A9E8D35314475BF4593135FCAD46F.description: A square with a side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

97B9118209524D748225A56903FB2331.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

CA1EB20802E14A2EB98374503FC3E658.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

4F84072B32814ECB8BA2EE2EB153BF92.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked in appropriate units—whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

B5C5695A75454AA18A394DA49983D9B5.description: Draw scaled picture graphs and scaled bar graphs to represent data sets with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

2DF17112012840FFA09CFA923D42665D.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units.

9749B68B7977420E8F076612CC972338.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve elapsed time word problems on the hour and the half hour, using a variety of strategies.

C93E9BF301CD42FD889336B4FBCFE72A.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

EEFF3E502F5543C382E3A4E0FBE2C2CF.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions by using a visual fraction model.

B2CF74D7CB98424C9684BEF0B0864E89.description: Recognize fractions, a/1 or a/a, that are equivalent to whole numbers. Express whole numbers as fractions, a/1 or a/a.

E71FEA6183544DEE82087DC1A17CA9A2.description: Explain why the fractions are equivalent using a visual fraction model.

913615A804D84B9983C50CA4D9700D63.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions.

35B92A79F29043818FAE0FB2C60846A5.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

07D9FC6C236545889C48DA9870C14D93.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

C6FAE165A46541869E42BEE70A631E20.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

EBB25B0C153F4B7E92DB0BAEA8E23129.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

6CE9E5D524F642E6BA98C60F4BFEA755.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

E7DAA463FC11453FB37738B8164DA9F9.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts. Understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by "a" parts of size 1/b.

1324EF930949430DBE91A16C2E51AE9E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

47E8529C0958495C89186FDCC7B6D90C.description: Using strategies based on place value and properties of operations, multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10-90.

1E5CCDC5B1D146CEB65A6779DD637541.description: Using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction, fluently add and subtract within 1000.

7B9D54F18B1A470E8163D1C98F1C5A96.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

4287F4A92F6648C09DB001123D8A22FD.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

240B7045BABA4818932C69773773C01A.description: Using mental strategies, fluently multiply and divide within 100.

2E078D00DAA342408A1AABC918F97367.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

03AB4D634C09406788F2ED5D92AC5013.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide (without the use of formal terms).

D5F8442DAFEB476D9DED4BF983FBF3C5.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

B5FF39AA1D124933BC4576E5E9948880.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

83A0A3CF9B91498B85E6C68C0C6150B4.description: Using drawings and equations with a symbol for an unknown number, solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.

A23BF0EC48934136957D440729FAF1A4.description: Interpret and model whole-number quotients of whole numbers, as the number in a group or the number of groups.

44E5AAE655BB41AC85E41BECD8E905C8.description: Interpret and model products of whole numbers.

1ED42C49595445259B6415A8C513A990.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

36178CFEE6F845D6A52FEFE024FF5B96.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

B7CD460A2686445EA1CDCEE19E88CF33.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

9C845EE783CB4A38B5F960709AEC2134.description: Using visual fraction models, explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b). CA28B30EFCC5434EBBF337FDDC72E4A9.description: Using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations, multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers. CC5B671644BE411BBBD02004A9985DAF.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers to the one millions place using strategies flexibly, including the standard algorithm.

DF1D86EC9BC94879B4713DEAA578390F.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

2979CE972B7B4951AF4E3A2413589324.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

A8A410AF5B7F4BD1A7B0C5D1EDB58B0A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
