E4F4A6F72303457590BBE684D1D7DB7C.description: Know and apply the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent.

925FF9534A514F73912FDB746CE3BED4.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find n(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

04F8D9614C8D43D19F232D14D642C106.description: Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

A298830D655F43BA842906E2B8C2560D.description: Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

98157CA2E3A542D6B1D94EA307ACB822.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

1B44E6090BCF48FC8FEDB8F3B93C3C5D.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions

59F22E9283CB4F4780FA0D8E731F9243.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

1A123BA1697B4E9EBA2A337CCA3AF99C.description: Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4 and π/6. (+) Use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x, in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

F98C2F984E5F4BEF8C669527E504882F.description: Extend right triangle trigonometry to the four quadrants. (+) Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

7078EE7D1F1C4F60B86BFCE61D210B6B.description: Understand that the radian measure of an angle is the ratio of the length of the arc to the length of the radius of a circle.

F01731C30BF946B1B90CD6D68F4EFE79.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circles

2EC70A32D5124C258BCEA1975E7E1A64.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear, quadratic, or exponential function in context.

D86622480ED64749B5882344B7C76150.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model

FECB925D8CAE4D6C8C0505A29B033634.description: Use logarithms to express the solution to ab<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are real numbers and b is a positive real number. Evaluate the logarithm using technology when appropriate.

5E3332C9F834483280BC6A8707A9AD05.description: Compare the end behavior of linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using graphs and/or tables to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing as a linear or quadratic function.

ECAA9167BBD94BD395F0B9E8CB6C142D.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a table, a description, or two input-output pairs given their relationship.

B5D7EFB229364ED29BAE04DE7788CFAC.description: Identify situations that can be modeled with linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. Justify the most appropriate model for a situation based on the rate of change over equal intervals. Include situations in which a quantity grows or decays.

D0C00249B71A429181579640F626695F.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems

A19A646DEE8C4480B9CE271E42798D4F.description: Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

19ABE968FA354828803F75CC3359DF13.description: Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

D865DB54545345DBA18E1B6C372C3CC6.description: Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

63BCCCB23C414949AA6A8913771DA86C.description: Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

D4A28CA30CEF4440A1360DB4B80F3FD9.description: Write an equation for the inverse given a function has an inverse.

F6019852C48C44908D4617C95314F29D.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, f(x + k), kf(x), and f(kx), for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Recognize even and odd functions from their graphs.

60BD600CDFF54ADEAD1053460A40022E.description: Build new functions from existing functions

44832ECA521E47DE9596081EA4D26A69.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula and convert between the two forms. Use sequences to model situations.

18BFDC751CF1426088185386F936122E.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

2534A3977B7B4CF5830E44BF7E045A43.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

4C331D7510D049CEA9D8F3ACD55413F3.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

AF376CCDADD446869C2DC91192959F08.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

17D1D1DF11FD4F9480307908C82731D4.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

C2818A6CE6DB4A2AA92D2DD84C47B9AD.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

01215664B98343F79E15422418F6D018.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

4BE106E77B7D4E68892B7D1943F7C412.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

32DC4D22140647009BC5805E1F6C0C3E.description: Graph trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, phase shift and amplitude.

0CB8AD0DF9054F37A3302184D333431E.description: Graph f(x) = sin x and f(x) = cos x as representations of periodic phenomena.

D04DBAADC3704F1B91252FA0BB503B29.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

66085BC3E8A446E1961C2F203F38ED54.description: Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

D8D7A19AB3284126AF59C9DB25150F46.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

A04C6E957966439BACE966FB9CCC8E0E.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

9A80719F6D79476097532E3960685F4F.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima where appropriate.

7C7582B9AC7D49719F39D9EB194DEA45.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

5298028876FA4589A9C98E365AA8C226.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

F6E1815A7A084F4EBB1B5C4FF46589CD.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

937FFEAEF4324E91BD83C8A4E26EBB49.description: Use tables, graphs, verbal descriptions, and equations to interpret and sketch the key features of a function modeling the relationship between two quantities.

1931B10DD9E74AFE9462A08ED7A3596E.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

51DBBEE7EF5D4B0CA7BE64F9AC8B2252.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers.

991E1D6BD72D4559AE35622505654726.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

DB574937158D4B9B8263D1CE30860597.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

2FBFBF4DCF5F4414AECDA28823B1703C.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

C6CEB0E4CDAD47A3B66FCCFEE07CEAB1.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A558865285954D448583DF8D6062851C.description: Look for and make use of structure.

A7DD6E189F604083AE6BC5295ACD44FE.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

2C2F976B9768478A971C53870609E78D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Dakota Mathematics Content Standards

B7ADD3BA8C59418586EDB7EEF4C92B44.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

34688654485B49B393071D85C63C9439.description: Calculating quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data was gathered.

F2B5CCAA98944F88B68D1A8E6809CEFF.description: Describing the nature of the attribute being investigated, including how it was measured and its units of measurement. Describe how the data was collected and what discrepancies may or may not exist.

41751E4F091F431DB12E2EF438DAF066.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context by:

A574E84EE14C4F1FAFF70621B31AE37B.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

CA98EB12D84F4E2EBC1B1CA2AC7E717E.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values using a single number, while a measure of spread (variation) describes how its values vary with a single number.

22FF9B2176A445FB832026B8FBBAEF14.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

13C947428BFE4C149290D127C68B593B.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

8530EA2C038D471C863AEE516E35EB0F.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real world problem that change in relationship to one another. Write an equation to express one quantity (dependent variable) in terms of the other quantity (independent variable). Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

3CEB4AAFC13E40A69BF285AABED17278.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

B0DD722FC4CF4440B0C80AF3D7AD603D.description: Write a statement of inequality of the form x > c or the form x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or the form x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

58270BD1555A423C8EE9E49B4154124B.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers.

D5574A47079D464884E13DF5EA6BFB94.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real world or mathematical problem. Understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

8FC492673AF847A69094A8C62612CD91.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: Which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

152005EEB3CC4F25B46DE8BE6AFD4A0A.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

C90A490620194B949D1FE433292DE91D.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.

3DC50855048D46FD9A6C30A760A0DEF0.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

5943C8D689A74EA995DE8767FBD463F3.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

E8DF24EF29844EE2A8F22F7863D516C5.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient, difference, quantity, etc.); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

908E465C2A364F0A83983C9285B18358.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

DE8B3E0BA6A44046BE4BAA5DC20D2F9C.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

83801EF4A75440A6839DC78AE8B24D6E.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

87E02B5A1FE845B3B357575C1425371D.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

4989E6D2F527408FA290BDFF84CDBB2C.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

23F730F8E5EC443B9ED48501302C408D.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

D24525EF9D0A46E399CA4AB36568C883.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line. Interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real world situation.

CDC8585DA0AE4961A0E484E2D22046D8.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real world contexts.

16B9C0E27D2C405F94D7AC675B851057.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

09B7BDD8E0B241DEBF317CCE59811FFB.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

F962F61B6B5D4339B2A7373DCB9FDB43.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram. Find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

7F5DCA720C9A406DB7862FE384DEC6A6.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane. Recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

D4523FB8ED2A454B95D67B7A788CBBA3.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line. Recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, for example: –(–3)=3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

4A645B0447254A5194F386745A9B0830.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

15E9BD49F9BE436D8B57C320C3825199.description: Understand that rational numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (may include temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, debits/credits, positive/negative electric charge, etc.). Use rational numbers to represent quantities in real world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

4BDE77C135B0452488330B558F673DEC.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

997B38C3E26941CFAF684193A1A41A19.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1 to 100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

DF1FF50609F54E658F0785D4BF68CA31.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using strategies flexibly, including the standard algorithm for each operation.

C2D03D65707A497690F9F298C6EAB3D4.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using strategies flexibly, including the standard algorithm.

27309F9136C94DED90F9976E0A318482.description: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

3809753A6CE040E8A189DA644C5A7EEA.description: Use visual fraction models and equations to interpret and compute quotients of fractions. Use models and equations to solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.

A914CA85CD434A7FB9C34A15ACB77F88.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

E3CAA93BA8EC496193F04E56E95E2568.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units. Manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

FBF30F683B8146AB9E51713BE4DFB147.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100. Solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

B1A4FF04C4D844F69EDA6F9F4EE5EC7B.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

FF8EB9861F734555A8388AF98616E07C.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

0471414F16D447EE8970CC73705CC1F6.description: Use tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, and equations to reason about ratios and rates in real world and mathematical problems.

12F7CF0C0D85401D8AAD78A9B5641C68.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

A2585209CD9440FCA0ABB618BE10FB00.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

D6B15031882B42BDBA088366CC304D91.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

6CACE4D680D34F6C9D3B08F18DCEB458.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles (right prisms and pyramids whose bases are triangles and rectangles). Use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

CAD6151665FE466E981F516BB6A6D891.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices. Use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

D34B9B2A55EF470C8F4A0EB8C4986A92.description: Using cubes of an appropriate size, pack a right rectangular prism having fractional edge lengths to find its volume. Then show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths of the prism. Apply the formulas V = lwh and V = Bh to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

57EA7F74E71446E6B550874F07A0C1C4.description: Based on prior knowledge of area of rectangles, decompose or compose triangles to find the area of a triangle. Using knowledge of area of triangles and rectangles, compose and/or decompose triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons to find their areas. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real world mathematical problems.

C9EEEA9E85184A9882851C02A322CBD7.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

C63B2E4900984A1AA0D94A364918BE35.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

C8F2C54F54BB4407B7E35C6A7FC346D1.description: Look for and make use of structure.

2B73E64BDFA84E3892E09C73689BF1C6.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

1528EB90EB7F4800B1B82B0E6170E81D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: North Dakota Mathematics Content Standards

E64AC19C68684712B8521CE2F766BF8F.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

0CF46656D9B947F583F72D7CF80A975F.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

97993CDD31C84D228C5130D3844BECFC.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

39A32D2E4380452896BA7620C3F02C8C.description: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations

056F10F5238A48C288FB8444B63337DB.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

0F5F95FC355B491EB007EB828F648F8B.description: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects

A0507D528C424FB8836F17E5B1DA4CB4.description: Know and apply volume formulas for prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

96D471C80A94453786A74E6A6049D1EE.description: Calculate the surface area for prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

E286D2DDBA8C48F5B7EDD5446A09B5AD.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

B73B613AA0F942ED972C37B45404AFBA.description: Explain surface area and volume formulas and use them to solve problems

D1CE3599759C4D4CB18BC69E4BD86F3C.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles, parallelograms, trapezoids and kites.

1DE67D31F33F4D44B6AFF67ACA47CFA6.description: Use coordinates to find the midpoint or endpoint of a line segment. (+) Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that (partitions the segment in a given ratio.

142C37D22F554340BFF46DD74D713326.description: Develop and verify the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines. Apply the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines to solve geometric problems using algebra.

C29AE30307264EDC90A3AF8522B7C39C.description: Use coordinates to verify simple geometric theorems algebraically. Use coordinates to verify algebraically that a given set of points produces a particular type of triangle or quadrilateral.

FD010BC1729A4FA28BD80AA10C7FB2F9.description: Use coordinates to verify simple geometric theorems algebraically

193F2A4D803A44AD9A29F1EDC8ADC7D3.description: Identify key features of conic sections given their equations. Apply properties of conic sections in real world situations.

246AD954A9094D8BB2E73EF2692915F9.description: Convert between the standard and general form equations of conic sections.

66210813CE214DFA915EEA4383101A3A.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius. Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix. (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

CD811A3EC6C640409ECF4123F5ECF66B.description: Explain and use the formulas for arc length and area of sectors of circles.

F18C14AC18E1482E80E20EE5647D0611.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles

3E2AEFB901EE491FA7BCD361A985A534.description: Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

76E6CB10BE094D148B708C663520F910.description: Construct the incenter and circumcenter of a triangle. Relate the incenter and circumcenter to the inscribed and circumscribed circles.

F6E44D962C0F4AF1AEE2D9F99B6B795A.description: Understand and apply theorems about relationships with angles formed by radii, diameter, secants, tangents, and chords. Understand and apply properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

F695726DF32F4C4AA316F0DC2A2017CB.description: Understand and apply theorems about relationships with line segments and circles including radii, diameter, secants, tangents, and chords.

201A296097F54E5B9850FBC6E7034F64.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles

1C0E14DB1F65474E84AD88D67436F606.description: Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in context.

2CD84C5B64394E78ADCA3B8D67D6C8AE.description: Solve unknown sides and angles of non-right triangles using the Laws of Sines and Cosines.

F405555CAACB439186EC1C0F6E69E570.description: Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

6571BCCB0605459CB43AE4D0E615D32A.description: Use special right triangles (30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90°), trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

4F4127BDF46D41D2A14D7C09A51908E7.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

4A778A5926DE454B885D9FA0ADB39345.description: Understand how the properties of similar right triangles allow the trigonometric ratios to be defined, and determine the sine, cosine, and tangent of an acute angle in a right triangle.

87067094CCC742618D3AADFD6467F75B.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

A0BD449B413A406AB076A33EFF20C9EE.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

5915517BEC2E4B298D63008DB27DDCB6.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

C27334E57C534FE2B13DAFB341E38305.description: Given two figures, use transformations to decide if they are similar. Apply the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

77F71E29C5944081A067998317104D58.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

086FDC51E8F244B2BD2009E6A8BA600D.description: Apply basic constructions to create polygons such as equilateral triangles, squares, and regular hexagons inscribed in circles.

945F759BE3D64C068BAF3B8E648C7CBB.description: Make basic geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods.

1FCF8D1980534B6686EBAB4D8DA9D1E4.description: Prove and apply theorems about parallelograms.

64642663151E4EB6BB0F7766211F823D.description: Prove and apply theorems about triangle properties.

1EA954AA9D8B4A3787BB198A3D3179CC.description: Prove and apply theorems about lines and angles.

84BBF7421EF845878C23E84ED2BDD863.description: Prove two triangles are congruent using the congruence theorems such as ASA, SAS, and SSS.

14B0A51C43B8452F8986032AF866E502.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

FD7CE6CB810448BABC183E523D630F2C.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure. Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if two figures are congruent.

E501DF4AA1674EA3ABDF32DDBEE378F2.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions

Students' narrative skills continue to grow in these grades. The Standards require that students be able to incorporate narrative elements effectively into arguments and informative/explanatory texts. In history/social studies, students must be able to incorporate narrative accounts into their analyses of individuals or events of historical import. In science and technical subjects, students must be able to write precise enough descriptions of the step-by-step procedures they use in their investigations or technical work that others can replicate them and (possibly) reach the same results.

26F22F3A27224D57B66CDEED5DBBCA55.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

968DD62FAE3F40A09B9B0FB19A2DD612.description: Narrative writing is not applicable as a separate requirement for history, social studies, science, and technical subjects. Students' narrative skills continue to grow in these grades. The Standards require that students be able to incorporate narrative elements effectively into arguments and informative/explanatory texts. In history/social studies, students must be able to incorporate narrative accounts into their analyses of individuals or events of historical import. In science and technical subjects, students must be able to write precise enough descriptions of the step-by-step procedures they use in their investigations or technical work that others can replicate them and (possibly) reach the same results.

D9FDF02DD1BE48B587568113D2B3D156.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly.

D4D5D1DEDC5B4D1BB7C618519F259EED.description: Narrative writing is not applicable as a separate requirement for history, social studies, science, and technical subjects. Students' narrative skills continue to grow in these grades. The Standards require that students be able to incorporate narrative elements effectively into arguments and informative/explanatory texts. In history/social studies, students must be able to incorporate narrative accounts into their analyses of individuals or events of historical import. In science and technical subjects, students must be able to write precise enough descriptions of the step-by-step procedures they use in their investigations or technical work that others can replicate them and (possibly) reach the same results.

B3A2B980EFD84948BB06D2C04D64D807.description: Narrative writing is not applicable as a separate requirement for history, social studies, science, and technical subjects. Students' narrative skills continue to grow in these grades. The Standards require that students be able to incorporate narrative elements effectively into arguments and informative/explanatory texts. In history/social studies, students must be able to incorporate narrative accounts into their analyses of individuals or events of historical import. In science and technical subjects, students must be able to write precise enough descriptions of the step-by-step procedures they use in their investigations or technical work that others can replicate them and (possibly) reach the same results.

B5768A9FC78849CBB744B944B0693045.description: Determine and apply appropriate formulas to solve right and non-right triangle problems in context.

C028139F414B48A8B961CDFAB8F52F80.description: Identify key features of a conic section given its equation. Apply properties of conic sections in context.

F38DEE313B6546C3A03FECDEA3F15D90.description: Write the equation of a conic section given its special features. Convert between the standard form and general form equations of conic sections.

B35458819CE74F5298BC086837D3C3AC.description: Know and apply the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent to solve problems.

7F506C9950EB47F3A5208EC6D77B04DA.description: Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions and interpret them in context.

E76C04F032A94C009356CFD415C47434.description: Restrict the domain of a trigonometric function to construct its inverse.

BA9B5B91FF6543A88B15BD23630F2FB1.description: Create a trigonometric function to model periodic phenomena.

679D8836FBE64BC89258AA9785DDDA09.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

2EA7D9BDF5A04863B4C689EE21B122F5.description: Use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

C19F1DB5EE97441A8B73809007C1CF76.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

A14D685A93C841F28A4AEAB05B23B52C.description: Use the Pythagorean Identity sin² (θ) + cos² (θ) = 1 to find sin (θ), cos (θ), or tan (θ) given sin (θ), cos (θ), or tan (θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

4F535418CA85476BA5B7453DBCB5F589.description: Extend right triangle trigonometry and apply knowledge of the unit circle to determine values of sine, cosine, and tangent for multiples of π/3, π/4, and π/6.

D6440D7413464FDBA583F5B7D292B4C0.description: Use properties of logarithms to express the solution to ab<sup>ct</sup> = d where a, c, and d are real numbers and b is a positive real number. Evaluate the logarithm using technology when appropriate.

CE9C31022AE54600B0195CADF7B51752.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula and convert between the two forms. Use sequences to model situations.

8381A69CD9EB48239A6F741D94B054CC.description: Determine whether a linear, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric model fits a situation. Determine an appropriate mathematical model in context (with or without technology).

95381963B2614E2C994E6F073972C952.description: Compare the end behavior of linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using graphs and/or tables to show that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing as a linear or quadratic function.

99E5518F395F41F6B6FD8E6ABEC20A1C.description: Graph trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, phase shift, and amplitude.

3D9C21C180CF4EB3A65AC6ACA7EAECE4.description: Graph rational functions, identifying domain, range, asymptote(s), removable and non-removable discontinuities, intercepts, behavior at the asymptote(s), and end behavior.

BC9017EF08914929B8F60C08A78C955E.description: Analyze and graph functions expressed symbolically (by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases), identifying key features of the graph.

7FBF058BB9B24B60A2C3EADE2BAC9F12.description: Graph f(x) = sin x and f(x) = cos x as representations of periodic phenomena.

AF77E4554C0142B38EEB4049345F4266.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

B74FC20E3977487AA2EEDE357A76E78F.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available and showing end behavior.

2875AE791CAC4C1E8D993F51729C613C.description: Graph square root, cube root, piecewise-defined, step, and absolute value functions.

7C44752DEAB744E6B7E8E0286EF9EE29.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

18B68A4562DF415BB0C72B00EDE3C5D3.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

63CC00684F1C4FCB8A163AEE7A23E666.description: Use tables, graphs, verbal descriptions, and equations to interpret and sketch the key features of a function modeling the relationship between two quantities.

62E3BF50758249708958A706527B7AAB.description: Compare key features of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically, in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

A795F73DDDAF496685E1096D62FA15AB.description: Apply the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms to solve problems.

1C157BCA120F409E805213246CE14C2F.description: Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

9CA1BF45ADD040FAABE5EAB45729C1B4.description: Recognize that the graph of a function and its inverse are reflection images over the line y = x.

96F91932B4D84F80ABDFE20BD575B5F7.description: Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

EC8A1824501F4CD2852D0F351F0E8954.description: Identify the effect of transformations on the graph of a function by replacing f(x) with af(x), f(bx), f(x - h), and f(x) + k, for specific values of a, h, and k (both positive and negative). Find the value of a, b, h, and k given the graph of the function. Recognize even and odd functions from their graphs and equations.

CBFF6DA20A41489487A81C38744DB0B7.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

A2F40EDF580A45FFAF0F5B1C964DDBAB.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, minimum/maximum, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of context.

7339E844E33E4BF4B51AF029D7D1C82E.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain the different properties of the function.

F68D6A3966534A1F8291696171358219.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

155739E338F84CB797275F0FEB06216A.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

8034FCC083A5465981269A61A0DAD4B8.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

9D6AC8479D6A43DD9159D7B3313A33BD.description: Apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (ax + by)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n and integers a and b.

692A224A60EF4665A0E02B2AFEF3AE7D.description: Solve a system of equations in three or more variables with matrices (using technology).

16B0C0D9C09E40119E3F60EAEF2A8B38.description: Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

21E27110503B457C8246BAC052D6D071.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.

1EDF37D3AD2042EC8A5F00DD958A21C4.description: Using graphs, technology, tables, or successive approximations, show that the solution(s) to the equation f(x) = g(x) are the x-value(s) that result in the y-values of f(x) and g(x) being the same.

EF0298B0C125463B810D884294A6D61D.description: Apply the Factor and Remainder Theorems to determine efficiently whether a linear expression is a factor of a polynomial equation. Apply the Remainder Theorem in context.

CE495FEA8C88476C8FD9984EB890CD52.description: Identify zeros of polynomial equations when suitable factorizations are available. Use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

9C89B49541F54510800C9FC504B0717C.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials beyond quadratics. Understand that polynomials form a system comparable to integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication.

BDF4A8F7740E4B09ADECB0A4207257D7.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable and identify extraneous solutions.

11CA8B1AE5444303A70EE15834B7E8B6.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have solutions of the form a + bi and a - bi.

E051D21DEFE6473F974E80F92210E90C.description: Derive the quadratic formula from the form 0 = ax² + bx + c.

3CBD31D5339447909E02CA0BD9AB8122.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities and by systems of equations and/or inequalities and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

08001A9F0E114DF4B4720A1C4F467697.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities. Graph equations on coordinate axes with proper labels and scales.

983125A5A67D464D9039B777039F07D2.description: Create equations and inequalities and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic equations and simple rational and exponential equations.

8A07783A57104090A088F0A963E60AFE.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms. Write a(x)/b(x) in the form of q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or technology for the more complicated examples.

594C57DBA0844E9898621F46A1F8FB9B.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions. Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression.

A164100F20E24C5E9E4DEBB7DAF70C6F.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to produce an equivalent expression.

16CD4F4E91734A4EB3A76A0BBEE7FF63.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform exponential expressions.

594205F5EB8942D7914D5E78FEC72376.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

9F65C1C790CD45218B02431A1B2B410E.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

064AC25013C84B3BBB73F19F8E3166AA.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

AF686FCCB49A47E8A837619BC5EDFE4C.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

8C3EC872632C4CF4AB82603954C8299C.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in context.

73910288FA6B402E9C29BE7153AE9F33.description: Use the structure of an expression (to extend to polynomial and rational expressions) to identify ways to rewrite it.

0C0414C2E31D42AA9B861BAE39B942D8.description: Rearrange multi-variable formulas to highlight a quantity of interest.

7BCCA69260A84F52BC4714E1878FE10A.description: Represent data in a matrix. Perform operations (i.e., addition, subtraction, multiplication) on matrices of appropriate dimensions to solve problems and in context. Know that matrix multiplication is not commutative.

51572304FCE144C18604625AF2D8112B.description: Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

47693FC06CE645EAA4448F7097B8DD79.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v.

573FEE5CA6BE492891B3DBB20836BC02.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction. Use the components to perform scalar multiplication (e.g., as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub> , cv<sub>y</sub>)).

76D1CA3E9F26444AAF0CFFCAB7BD2AC8.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

DA944848E6E74BA8AC465E7CBF54BAAC.description: Understand that vector subtraction v-w is defined as v+(-w), where -w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction.

97C53CDD81E642FD8FA7B6D7513B86FE.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

A4C32CA9FDC74A3F9EDC1ADF7015CDDB.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Know that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

68C3BC6D9AD54C3983EF88CB7FD70665.description: Add and subtract vectors. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order and using the components to perform vector subtraction.

9438E13BDC384205AF7186D81324DA58.description: Solve problems involving magnitude and direction that can be represented by vectors.

D8FBAB641CC8493A897869F21761A153.description: Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

71E2C76F0F304552927699399E30F2C9.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction, writing them in polar form.

5517CB8CF41745C7BC3DD4154140869E.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to find all roots of a polynomial equation and determine the nature (i.e., integer, rational, irrational, real, complex) of the roots.

D1B3B7DF51984F44AE91F31C4DEC664E.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

26531B614F384571A0A2BBDA8D64FE21.description: Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, conjugation, powers, and roots of complex numbers geometrically on the complex and/or polar plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

D2F2E3A251914FA5B42ED42EA6C0BCA8.description: Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular, trigonometric, and polar forms. Find the modulus (absolute value) of a complex number. Explain why the rectangular, trigonometric, and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

48D02ACBA707407E80E3E5E21FB7E1AD.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to determine the number of zeros for polynomial functions.

6A68255EFC804F31B2267B013ED27381.description: Use conjugates to find quotients of complex numbers.

9FE8174D1B564CF7ABA2BB6141B911FF.description: Use the definition i² = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

F5926DADA7C84BAF875B79A02D9D4ACB.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = -1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real. Understand the hierarchal relationships among subsets of the complex number system.

DD0256EDBF0440D19894B7629D370AB8.description: Choose a level of accuracy or precision appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

6534A586DCE34424B88CF7CE5B7D406F.description: Use units to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems (e.g., unit analysis). Choose and interpret units consistently in formulas. Choose and interpret the scale and the units in graphs and data displays.

DE97CA7D38894CEAA0EF461E13ACF73A.description: Demonstrate that the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational, and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

49C141C159B14E9284F62595B481BEA5.description: Perform operations on complex radical expressions and simplify radicals to write equivalent expressions.

46D690F729FE41B4AE808D0D86122464.description: Learners can reason logically, citing evidence to critique and explain what they see, think, and conclude through exploration, generalization, and validation.

D0FB65A8FCD145CE9B9B0FA15B614671.description: Learners can create connections within and across concepts, using supporting evidence to interpret how they originate, extend, and relate to other learning, ideas, and life experiences.

D7211673B0F6415F9FD397F94ED42CD2.description: Learners can analyze, execute, critique, and adapt approaches and solutions when problem-solving in novel situations.
